item.title: A Note From the Workshop
item.description:
This is a sample post. Replace it with a thought, a project update, or something you have learned recently.

Start with one idea

A good post does not need to cover everything. Pick one idea, explain why it matters, and give the reader enough context to follow along.

Clear writing starts with knowing what you want to say.

You can emphasize a phrase with bold text, add a little nuance with italics, or mention a command such as hugo server inline.

item.title: Learning in Public, One Note at a Time
item.description:
When learning something new, it is tempting to wait until you understand every detail before writing about it. That can mean never writing anything down at all.

Small notes are a better place to start. Capture the question you had, what you tried, and what finally made sense. The explanation can be imperfect; you can improve it the next time you return to the subject.

A simple note-taking loop

  1. Write down one question you want to answer.
  2. Try a small example and record what happened.
  3. Summarize the useful part in your own words.

Over time, these notes become a record of your progress and a practical reference for your future self. Sharing them can help someone else who is asking the same question.

item.title: Starting a Blog with Hugo
item.description:
This blog is built with Hugo, a static site generator that turns content files and templates into a site of plain HTML, CSS, and other assets.

Posts live in Markdown files under content/posts/. Each one begins with front matter for its title, date, tags, and publication status. The Paper theme supplies the layouts that turn those files into pages.

To preview the site locally, run hugo server from the directory containing hugo.toml. Hugo watches the content files and refreshes the preview when they change.
